title: Purchase approval decision map (capex vs opex) - 1:1 prep (scratchpad)
content:
Context:
- Quick prep for my 1:1 with Ben (finance lead) — need a crisp decision framework for a ~8–12 GPU cluster procurement request from Serving Runtime team.
- Ask from infra: dedicated on-prem-ish cluster (customer demo/staging and internal heavy evals) — quoted options from vendors and a cloud reserved alternative.
- Primary tension: treat as CapEx (buy hardware) vs Opex (reserved cloud/Dedicated capacity). Need sign-off path and suggested fallback if leadership wants to push to hosted.

Objectives for the 1:1:
1) Get explicit decision criteria we will use (thresholds, payback horizon, procurement timeline constraints).
2) Confirm approval authority levels (who signs >$100k / >$250k / >$500k).
3) Agree financing path (CapEx purchase vs lease vs Opex contract) and accounting treatment.
4) Identify negotiation levers and next steps owners.

Summary of options (high level):
- Option A: CapEx purchase (on-prem racks)
  - Upfront: ~$370k (8x A100-80GB equivalent + networking + rack + support) — vendor quotes vary.
  - Ongoing: minimal monthly infra ops (~$6k/mo).
  - Accounting: capital asset, depreciate over 3 years.
  - Pros: potentially lowest long-run unit cost for sustained load; full control for private deployments.
  - Cons: large headroom spend now; lead time 6–10 weeks; maintenance burden; risk of underutilization for Q2 spikes.

- Option B: Opex (Reserved Dedicated / Cloud committed capacity)
  - Upfront: ~$0–40k (commitment deposit depending on vendor).
  - Monthly: ~$35k–50k committed, depending on region and committed hours.
  - Accounting: expense; cleaner for short-term budgets.
  - Pros: faster to spin up, lower initial CAPEX, easier to scale down, vendor managed.
  - Cons: higher per-token cost long-term; subject to provider price variance; less control for private workloads.

- Option C: Hybrid / Lease / Financing
  - Spread CapEx cost via 36-month lease — preserves capita headroom, cheaper than cloud in long run if utilization high.
  - Need vendor financing terms, check interest, security.

Run-rate impact (back-of-envelope):
- Current hosted spend for these workloads: ~$150k/month (peak test + eval + demos).
- If we migrate sustained evals/demos to owned cluster: estimated net reduction in hosted fees by ~$90–120k/month after stabilization (assumes 70% of current hosted load is portable).
- Payback (CapEx): ~3–4 months of saved hosted spend to net the capital outlay? That feels optimistic — double-check utilization assumptions.
- Conservative scenario (50% portable): payback ~6–9 months.
- Note: need to include ops headcount time (~0.2 FTE) and electricity/colocation in monthly ops.

Procurement approval checklist (draft):
- Business justification doc (serving-runtime: INFRA-762) — ✓ in ticket but expand ROI section.
- Vendor quotes (min 3) — have 2 so far (Vendor A, Vendor B).
- Total cost of ownership model (3yr) — draft in spreadsheet (link in linked_artifacts).
- Delivery lead times and SLA for parts/support — ask vendors for 5yr NBD support pricing.
- Security / compliance signoff (infosec) — flag for private deployment.
- Funding source identified (CapEx pool vs operating budget) — need Ben's preference.
- Approval routing map: PO by procurement -> procurement director -> finance vp -> CFO (thresholds to confirm).

Questions I need Ben to answer / confirm in 1:1:
- What are the hard approval thresholds for our current fiscal policy? (who signs $250k+, $500k+)
- Is leadership comfortable moving budget from Hosted API line to a CapEx purchase this quarter?
- If we go hybrid/lease, do we have existing vendor financing contracts or preferred lessors?
- Risk tolerance on lead time: if vendor lead time pushes demos out, do we accept temporary cloud burst costs?
- Any preference for accounting (CapEx vs Opex) from a tax/forecasting standpoint?

Negotiation points / vendor asks I want sign-off to push on:
- Better MSRP on GPUs if we commit to 2+ clusters (volume discount).
- Longer support window (5yr) and spare parts SLA included.
- Include initial install and racking at no charge.
- Trade-in or buyback after 36 months to limit EOL risk.
- Vendor financing (0% for first 12 months?) — need the team to explore.

Open risks and mitigation:
- Underutilization risk: propose reserving some capacity to internal experiments and paid partner demos.
- Rapid model changes might require different GPU types — mitigate with vendor trade-in clause or modular chassis.
- Capital tied up could constrain Q3 go-to-market experiments — consider phased procurement (4 GPU nodes now, add 4 later).

Decision framework proposal (for the 1:1):
- If expected utilization >60% (3yr avg) and payback <12 months => prefer CapEx.
- If payback 12–24 months or utilization uncertain => prefer Lease/Hybrid.
- If immediate time-to-market <6 weeks required and budget constrained => Opex (reserved).
- Need Ben's approval on these thresholds or adjustments.

Immediate follow-ups (action items - rough):
- Aisha: bake conservative utilization sensitivity into TCO model; add electricity + colocation + 0.2 FTE ops to monthly ops. Due: 2025-02-24.
- Jordan (infra lead): push for 3rd vendor quote and confirm 6-week and 10-week delivery scenarios. Due: 2025-02-21.
- Raja (procurement): map approval routing and confirm who signs at $250k / $500k levels; check vendor financing partners. Due: 2025-02-22.
- Ben: confirm approval thresholds and high-level preferred financing (CapEx vs Opex) in 1:1. Due: next 1:1 meeting (2025-02-20).
- Infra/Product: produce short risk mitigation plan for model churn (modular nodes, trade-in). Due: 2025-03-01.

Notes to self / scratch points:
- Double-check depreciation schedule: 3yrs straight line vs 5yrs — which is our current policy for infra? (ask accounting).
- Host cost reduction estimate likely inflated — re-run with 50% portable assumption.
- Remember to reference INFRA-762 and INV-301 during the 1:1 — Ben likes seeing tickets in context.
- If Ben prefers Opex, prepare a fallback one-pager that compares reserved cloud cost vs Redwood Dedicated commit.

Slack refs/places to update after 1:1:
- Post summary to #finance-procurement with final decision and next steps.
- Ping @procurement-team and @infra-leads with vendor ask list.

Draft 2-sentence exec ask (for email to leadership once Ben signs off):
"Requesting approval to pursue procurement path for a dedicated GPU cluster for serving/runtime demos and sustained internal evals. We propose [CapEx purchase / Lease / Opex reserved] based on utilization forecast; attached TCO model shows payback under conservative assumptions in X–Y months and recommends phased rollout to reduce risk."

Unresolved items to bring to 1:1 if time allows:
- Confirm whether existing committed cloud contracts have termination penalties that would affect migration economics.
- Confirm which budget owner should absorb the early-month hosted overrun if lead time slips.
- Any tax or capital planning events in the next quarter that would change depreciation preference.

End of scratchpad.
(Will clean and convert the TCO figures into a polished 1-pager after Ben confirms thresholds in the 1:1.)
